content: ब्राह्मण {%a.%} (-णी|{%f.%}) [ब्रह्म वेदं शुद्धं चैतन्यं वा वेत्त्वधीते वा अण्] .²1 Belonging to a Brāhmaṇa. .²2 Befitting a Brāhmaṇa. .²3 Given by a Brāhmaṇa. .²4 Relating to religious worship. .²5 One who knows Brahma. .{@-णः@} .²1 A man belonging to the first of the four original castes of the Hindus, a Brāhmaṇa (born from the mouth of the {%Puruṣa%}); ब्राह्मणोऽस्य मुखमासीत् <ls>Rv. 10. 90. 12</ls>; <ls>Ms. 1. 31</ls>, <ls n="Ms. 1.">96</ls>; (जन्मना ब्राह्मणो ज्ञेयः संस्कारैर्द्विंज उच्यते . विद्यया याति विप्रत्वं त्रिभिः श्रोत्रिय उच्यते .. or जात्या कुलेन वृत्तेन स्वाध्यायेन श्रुतेन च . एभिर्युक्तो हि यस्तिष्ठोन्नित्यं स द्विज उच्यते ..). .²2 A priest, theologian. .²3 An epithet of Agni. .²4 <ab>N.</ab> of the twenty eighth Nakṣatra. .{@-णम्@} .²1 An assemblage or society of Brāhmaṇas. .²2 That portion of the Veda which states rules for the employment of the hymns at the various sacrifices, their origin and detailed explanation, with sometimes lengthy illustrations in the shape of legends or stories. It is distinct from the {%Mantra%} portion of the Veda. .²3 <ab>N.</ab> of that class of the Vedic works which contain the Brāhmaṇa portion (regarded as Śruti or part of the revelation like the hymns themselves). Each of the four Vedas has its own Brāhmaṇa or Brāhmaṇas:-- ऐतरेय or आश्वलायन and कौषीतकी or सांख्यायन belonging to the Ṛgveda; शतपथ to the Yajurveda; पञ्चविंश and षड्विंश and six more to the Sāmaveda, and गोपथ to the Atharvaveda. .²4 The Soma vessel of the Brahman priest.
